summary.text: Patient 1 is a female patient aged 89 years. Diabetes is recorded as present, and urinary instrumentation is recorded as absent. A past urinary tract infection is recorded as present, and a past resistant urinary tract infection as present. The admitting diagnosis category was other.

The urine culture was positive for ESBL-producing Gram-negative bacteria, and the organism is listed as Proteus mirabilis. The isolate was resistant to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin, sensitive to piperacillin–tazobactam and meropenem, sensitive to amikacin and resistant to gentamicin. Positive blood cultures are recorded as No.

The patient was initially treated in the emergency department, was considered stable there and did not require vasopressors or intensive fluid resuscitation. The hospital-at-home stay lasted 3 days, with amikacin as the home antibiotic, and the patient did not die at home during the hospital-at-home days. Acute kidney injury is recorded as present.
At discharge the patient showed clinical improvement, and inflammatory markers improved. At 30 days the table records no recurrent UTI, no re-admission, and death recorded.

summary.text: Patient 10 is a male patient aged 88 years. Diabetes is recorded as absent, and urinary instrumentation is recorded as absent. A past urinary tract infection is recorded as present, and a past resistant urinary tract infection as present. The admitting diagnosis category was lower urinary tract infection.

The urine culture was positive for ESBL-producing Gram-negative bacteria, and the organism is listed as Escherichia coli. The isolate was resistant to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin, sensitive to piperacillin–tazobactam and meropenem, intermediate to amikacin and sensitive to gentamicin. Positive blood cultures are recorded as No.

The patient was initially treated in the emergency department, was considered stable there and did not require vasopressors or intensive fluid resuscitation. The hospital-at-home stay lasted 7 days, with ertapenem as the home antibiotic, and the patient did not die at home during the hospital-at-home days. Acute kidney injury is recorded as absent.
At discharge the patient showed clinical improvement, and inflammatory markers improved. At 30 days the table records recurrent UTI not available, no re-admission, and no death.

article_limitations: Retrospective case series reported as one table with a column per patient; patient numbers are the table column numbers and no narrative per patient is given.

Cohort sentences (cause of death, cause of re-admission, AKI resolution, non-urinary admitting diagnoses, fever in the emergency department, impaired cognition, direct versus delayed HAH admission) are not attributed to individual patients because they name no patient.

Text says E. coli was the most common pathogen in seven out of nine patients, while the Table 1 genus row lists E in seven of eleven columns; the denominator differs and is left unreconciled. Small percentage differences between abstract and body (for example 27.2% vs 27.3%, 77.7% vs 77.8%, 36.3% for 4 of 11) are rounding.
The text pronoun his for the single patient with a positive blood culture conflicts with the female gender listed for the column with that blood culture; recorded as an ambiguity only.

The abstract says 57% had diabetes mellitus, while the Results give four out of eleven (36.3%) and Table 1 lists four Yes cells; this is a cohort-level discrepancy with no per-patient value in dispute, so the table cells are kept.

The Discussion says there were no cases of recurrent UTIs during the 30-day follow-up, while the Results and Table 1 give three patients as not available; the table value is kept and the discrepancy is recorded as an ambiguity on those patients.

The Methods say all cases referred to HAH were indicated for completion of intravenous antibiotics, while the Results say two patients were not treated with antibiotics and Table 1 lists two NONE cells.

Temporal relations use only sentences that state the pathway for all patients: initial emergency department treatment before the HAH stay, the HAH stay before discharge, the home antibiotic during the HAH stay and after the urine culture result it was tailored to, and the 30-day outcomes after discharge. No per-patient time is given; the 30-day outcome facts keep only their row-label wording with relation unknown.
Blood culture cells reading No are recorded as the literal cell value without a negative flag because the source does not state that blood cultures were drawn for every patient.
Table 1 ages carry no stated reference time, so they are recorded as age_other.
The source has no figures and no supplementary material (raw XML checked).
